Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Tools, fasteners & household repair

dull adjective

blunt, not sharp

also blunt, not sharp, dull (of a person), sluggish, be sluggish

classical

Ov. A.A. 3.589
Cic. Har. Resp. 2: tēla … hebetiōra (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 307, 151, 158

hebes, hebetis

adjective, third declension, one ending · Wiktionary

blunt, dull

Blunt, as against acūtus; also, of the mind or senses, dull, slow (Gell. 4.19.1).

Other words

  • obtūsus, obtūsa, obtūsum — blunted; dulled

    also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 7.3.5: obtūsus … stomachus · Declension on Wiktionary

    The participle of obtundere, “beat blunt”.

  • hebeō, hebēre — to be blunt; to be dull, sluggish

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Verg. A. 5.396 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 158 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

Examples

  • Pōnite jam gladiōs hebetēs: pugnētur acūtīs.

    Put away the blunt swords now: let the fight be with sharp ones.Ov. A.A. 3.589

  • Quaesō, ut apparēs mihi pennam hanc. — Deest mihi gladiolus scrīptōrius. — Ēn tibi. — Hui, quam obtūsus!

    Please trim this pen for me. — I haven’t got a penknife. — Here you are. — Goodness, how blunt it is!Erasm. Coll., Euntēs in lūdum litterārium

See also knife, be bored.
